title: dedicated: enforce throughput guarantees with burst token-bucket controls and utilization reporting
author: Ravi Kapoor
description: Motivation: Dedicated customers require predictable per-tenant throughput while allowing short bursts to absorb traffic spikes. This PR implements a token-bucket based burst control in the Dedicated fleet autoscaler and surfaces per-fleet and per-tenant utilization reporting in the Console to validate guarantees. Summary: 1) Add token-bucket rate limiter to the fleet autoscaler to enforce steady-state throughput guarantees with configurable burst capacity and replenishment rates. 2) Integrate utilization metrics (token consumption, burst usage, refill rate) into the metrics pipeline and add dashboard panels and API endpoints for per-fleet/per-tenant visibility. 3) Provide a migration script to backfill burst defaults for existing fleets and an example burst profile config. 4) Add unit and integration tests and documentation describing knobs and rollout plan. Backwards compatibility: default burst profile matches current behavior (no effective throttle) unless operator config sets non-zero burst caps. Rollout: feature gated behind flags, incremental rollout to 20% of fleets, monitor token burn and queueing metrics for 72h before wider rollout. Related: ENG-1987 implements the high-level autoscaling policy; follows up on several earlier burst reporting PRs. Checklist: - [x] token-bucket algorithm implemented and unit tested - [x] metrics emitted for token consumption and burst events - [x] Console panels + API endpoints added - [x] migration script and example config included - [x] docs updated - [x] integration tests for steady-state and burst scenarios Testing: unit tests for token refill logic and concurrent drains added; integration tests simulate sustained load and sudden spikes to validate throughput guarantees and fallback behavior when burst exhausted. Observability: added histograms and counters with tags (fleet_id, tenant_id, model_variant). Rollback plan: flip feature flag and migrate configs back; consumers will see restored pre-change behavior.
